A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

our method is able to reproduce, in a satisfactory way, the observed spectral energy distributions of the galaxies, with the advantage of being able to quantify uncertainties on the recovered parameters.

our method provides a good estimate of the star formation history, with a reasonable uncertainty on the age bins and the extinction, while the metallicity can be only inferred when the stellar population shows an old age.
our model can be successfully applied to a wide variety of galaxies, including early-type galaxies and star-forming systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stellar content can be inferred with high reliability, even when extinction and/or metallicity are not.
the extinction law is not constant with age, but that the extinction is higher for the youngest stars, in agreement with the theoretical predictions.
the uncertainties in the recovered parameters are a fundamental piece of information for a reliable interpretation of the results.
